points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once (e.g. once when the function is called, at program start, or at compile time). Accept equivalent wording such as 'static array gets initialized a single time'.

States that a non-static (ordinary local/automatic) array is initialized every time the function is called / each time control reaches its declaration. Accept 'reinitialized on every call' or 'created fresh each call'.
States the resulting difference: a static array retains its values between function calls, whereas a non-static array does not (its values are lost/recreated on each call).

levels.says: Mentions retention of values for the static array or loss/recreation for the non-static array, but not both sides of the contrast.

rubric.notes: Full marks require saying that a static array is initialized only once and contrasting it with a non-static array, which is initialized on every function call, so the static array keeps its values between calls. Part marks are given for only one side of the contrast or for the retention/loss consequence without the initialization-frequency contrast. No marks for answers that do not mention initialization frequency or that confuse static with const/global.
